_comment: One entry per feature artifact. `slug` matches parts/<slug>.html and pages/<slug>.html. `url` is filled in after the first publish so a rebuild redeploys to the same artifact.

features.title: Platform Foundations
features.lede: One repo, two deployable apps, nine shared values, and a clone that runs with zero credentials.
features.description: How the monorepo, split settings, shared constants, the single fetch funnel and the two deploys hold the rest of the product up.

features.title: The Ten Tables
features.lede: Every row the product keeps, what it is the only place to learn, and the four columns V1 had that V2 refused.
features.description: The data model: ten tables, their keys and constraints, and why each departure from V1 was made.

features.title: Machines On Both Sides
features.lede: The flow lives in transition tables — three on the server, eighteen in the browser — and nothing else decides.
features.description: The orchestration layer: dispatch, guards, actions through deps, and the frontend's five-file split.

features.title: Catalogue And Landing
features.lede: The public face: what an anonymous visitor is served, and where the book's own bytes come from.
features.description: GET /api/books, cover and sample endpoints, and the landing page that leads with the idea of reading this way.

features.title: Razorpay Checkout
features.lede: Money arrives twice — once on the redirect, once on the webhook — and exactly one reader comes out.
features.description: Standard Checkout, the two fulfilment legs, and the idempotency that keeps a double signal from making a second reader.

features.title: Onboarding And Entitlement
features.lede: One door a reader comes through, one question about whether they may read, and four identity cases decided in advance.
features.description: create_reader and can_read: the two seams that make payments and cadence drop-ins rather than second implementations.

features.title: Login And Session
features.lede: A cookie on the parent domain, rehydrated on boot, and the failure that localhost can never show you.
features.description: Session endpoints, SessionAuth, CSRF policy, and the root machine region that decides who is looking.

features.title: Credentials And Recovery
features.lede: No email provider, so a password is set and recovered over WhatsApp — single-use, cooled down, and mute about who exists.
features.description: Set-a-password, reset over WhatsApp, single-use tokens and the row-counted cooldown.

features.title: Profile And Account
features.lede: The reader's own page: what they may change, what that costs elsewhere, and the row every change leaves behind.
features.description: GET/PATCH /api/profile, password change, the AccountChange audit row, and the identicon in the header.

features.title: The Cadence Tick
features.lede: The product's first sentence: the schedule is rows minted at purchase, and a cron job fires whatever is due.
features.description: cadence.schedule, cadence.tick, the Render cron job, and why a double tick delivers once.

features.title: WhatsApp Delivery
features.lede: One mechanism, named wrappers, and a send that returns rather than raises — because a hiccup at Twilio is not a refund.
features.description: whatsapp.send_chapter, the template config, MessageLog's lifecycle, bounded retry and the console backend.

features.title: Grants And Sanctuary
features.lede: A link that authenticates by itself, dies after seven days, and lands a week-late reader somewhere kind.
features.description: Mint-or-reuse, GrantAuth, derived expiry, the opening page, and one-tap reissue from sanctuary.

features.title: The Reading Chamber
features.lede: The PDF never reaches the browser. Pages are rendered once, watermarked on every request, and served as images.
features.description: services/pages.py, the page_layout record, the per-request watermark, and the chamber that renders it.

features.title: Reading Progress
features.lede: Where the reader is, kept quietly, and deliberately wired to nothing that decides access.
features.description: ReadingProgress, the two idempotent writes, and the line that keeps unlocks schedule-driven.

features.title: The Home Shelf
features.lede: The reader's own library: no tokens in the payload, dates instead of countdowns, and a link that mints on demand.
features.description: GET /api/home, the selectors behind it, and the home page machine's two parallel regions.

features.title: The Companion Panel
features.lede: A chapter-scoped discussion partner that asks you questions, holds the whole chapter in its prompt, and never interrupts.
features.description: Extraction, the capped service, ChatUsage as the counter, the provider switch, and the panel that speaks first.

features.title: Reader Stewardship
features.lede: The owner's side of a reader: create, correct, deactivate, erase — and why removing is not deleting.
features.description: StaffAuth, the admin reader API, and the in-app admin screens that replaced Django admin.

features.title: The Book Workspace
features.lede: Drop a folder of PDFs and watch them become chapters: signed uploads straight to R2, auto-matched, fixed by drag.
features.description: catalog.py and uploads.py, the three-step upload, chapter auto-matching, and the rules that protect readers of a published book.

features.title: Covers And Video
features.lede: Cover bytes are proxied like everything else. Video is the one exception, and it is bounded on purpose.
features.description: services/media.py: proxied covers, short-lived signed video URLs, and the free-tier arithmetic behind the exception.

features.title: The Jewel Surface
features.lede: One stylesheet is the source of truth, four colours with two shades each, and nothing glows.
features.description: The palette and type tokens, the theme script, motion rules, skeletons and the site header.

features.title: Commands And Operations
features.lede: Everything a human can do, a function does — and every function has a command that calls it.
features.description: seed_dev, send_chapter, cadence_tick, render_chapters, machine_diagram, and where the logs go.
